run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T14:46:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by the rollout restart of the ad Deployment at 2026-11-16T14:45:27Z. The replacement ad pod was marked Ready at 14:45:29 (its container defines no readiness or startup probe) but its process logged "Ad service starting." only at 14:50:09.97Z and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 14:51:49.97Z, and its first request-handling lines appear at 14:53:11Z; ad counted no oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans across the four 2-minute buckets ending 14:48–14:54. In that gap the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans failed fast (398.89 of 445.56 error spans at or under 2 ms) and its GET /api/data handler returned errors one-for-one with them (428.06 error spans each over 19 minutes), which is what the alert measures. A second, shorter contributor was the simultaneous restart of the payment Deployment at 14:45:26Z: checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error spans (77.63 each) produced the frontend's POST /api/checkout errors, and payment counted no Charge server spans in the bucket ending 14:48. frontend-proxy ingress and router frontend egress error spans rose in the same buckets (116 and 117.33). The frontend pod itself was never restarted (running from 14:12:41Z, restartCount 0); all 21 deployments currently report 1/1 ready. Heavy CFS throttling of the new ad container during startup (about 18–20 throttled periods/s versus at most 1.37/s on the previous pod) is consistent with, but does not prove, that the 50m CPU limit lengthened startup. Why ad and payment were rolled out could not be determined because change history is not integrated, and the alert rule's exact expression could not be read.

claims.text: In the 19-minute window ending 15:05:16Z, frontend span totals were STATUS_CODE_ERROR 2035.7 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 30100.8; the error spans were GET /api/data 428.06, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 428.06, executing api route (pages) /api/data 428.06, POST /api/checkout 77.63, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 77.63, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 77.63 and tcp.connect 12.94.

Nonzero STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases in the 19-minute window were returned only for frontend (2035.69), frontend-proxy (1026.47: ingress 525.10 and router frontend egress 501.37), checkout (155.26: oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 77.63 and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 77.63), ad (1.33 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean) and recommendation (1.08 on flagd EventStream); payment returned 0 for its GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect error series.

The frontend GET /api/data STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter was flat at 346 from 14:00 until it began increasing at 14:46, reached 747 by 14:55 and stayed 747 through the last point at 15:01; the matching STATUS_CODE_UNSET counter rose normally to 1434 by 14:42, stayed flat until 14:55, then resumed rising (1454 at 14:57, 1567 at 15:01).

At 15-second resolution the frontend GET /api/data error counter first increased at 14:46:15 (8 spans) and again at 14:46:30 (8), then in larger bursts at 14:49:55 (126), 14:51:35 (78), 14:52:35 (120) and 14:53:35 (112).

The ad Deployment was rolled out at 14:45:27Z: ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d (revision 2, created 14:45:27) carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:45:27Z and is otherwise identical to ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, AD_PORT 8080, cpu limit 50m, memory limit 450Mi), and events show SuccessfulCreate of pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 at 14:45:27 plus Killing and SuccessfulDelete of pod ad-554b849958-6z62j at 14:45:29.

The ad container spec defines no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, so the new pod's Ready condition became True at 14:45:29Z while the container was still starting; the ad container is still on a single instance (startedAt 14:45:29Z, restartCount 0, empty lastState).

The new ad container's own log shows "Ad service starting." at 14:50:09.97Z and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 14:51:49.97Z, with the first request-handling lines ("Targeted ad request received ...", "no baggage found in context") at 14:53:11Z and later.

Ad's own server spans stopped during the outage: increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="ad",span_name="oteldemo.AdService/GetAds",status_code="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"}) was 60–86.7 per 2 minutes up to the bucket ending 14:46, 0 for the buckets ending 14:48, 14:50, 14:52 and 14:54, and 82.67 for the bucket ending 14:56; getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds follow the same pattern.

The failed frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans failed fast: of 445.56 error spans in the 10 minutes ending 14:55:16Z, 398.89 were at or under 2 ms, 420.0 at or under 4 ms, 421.11 at or under 10 ms and 437.78 at or under 100 ms, whereas the pre-incident successful GetAds spans (10 minutes ending 14:40) were mostly 10–200 ms (423.16 at or under 10 ms, 446.32 at or under 50 ms, 508.42 at or under 200 ms of 540 total).

The new ad pod was heavily CPU-throttled while starting: rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) was 10.1–19.9 per second for pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 over 14:46–14:53 (peak 19.88 at 14:51), versus 0.27–1.37 per second for the previous pod ad-554b849958-6z62j; container CPU usage was 0.048–0.099 cores for the new pod versus 0.005–0.012 cores for the old one.

The payment Deployment was also restarted at 14:45:26Z: ReplicaSet payment-5d565cf9b (revision 2) carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:45:26Z with no readiness, liveness or startup probe; its pod started at 14:45:30Z (Ready True since 14:45:30Z, restartCount 0), and events show SuccessfulCreate at 14:45:26 with Killing and SuccessfulDelete of the old pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp at 14:45:30.

payment counted no grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server spans in the 2-minute bucket ending 14:48 (increase 0), then 56 in the bucket ending 14:50 and 54.7 in each of the two following buckets; the payment container log lines returned for 14:45:20–14:52:00 begin at 14:51:06 with "Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete." pairs.

frontend-proxy error spans follow the same window: ingress errors were 0 in the bucket ending 14:46 and earlier, then 116 (bucket ending 14:48), 52, 76, 81.33 and 2.67; router frontend egress errors were 117.33, 52, 74.67 and 0 for the same buckets.

All 21 deployments in otel-demo currently report readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, and the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg has been running since 14:12:41Z with restartCount 0 and Ready True since 14:12:42Z.

The newest frontend traces Jaeger returned for 14:00–14:46:30 all start at 14:30:02.69–14:30:03.29Z; that sample shows the parent-child edges frontend GET /api/data to executing api route (pages) /api/data to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds to ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, and checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge to payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.

Primary cause: the ad Deployment's 14:45:27 rollout removed the only ad replica and replaced it with a pod that was Ready at 14:45:29 but whose gRPC server only began listening at 14:51:49 and only served requests from 14:53 onward; with no readiness or startup probe gating the Service, the frontend's GetAds calls were routed to a non-listening endpoint and failed in under 2 ms, making GET /api/data return errors and driving the frontend error-rate alert.

Secondary contributor: the payment Deployment's 14:45:26 restart left checkout without a serving payment endpoint at the start of the window (no payment Charge server spans in the 14:46–14:48 bucket), which produced checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error spans and the frontend's POST /api/checkout errors (77.63 error spans, present only in the 14:47 and 14:49 buckets).

The ad container's 50m CPU limit likely lengthened its startup: the new ad pod was throttled at about 18–20 CFS periods/s and used 0.048–0.099 cores between 14:46 and 14:53, versus at most 1.37 throttled periods/s and 0.005–0.012 cores on the old pod, and its application log begins only at 14:50:09 although the container started at 14:45:29.

The frontend-proxy error spans are most plausibly the proxy-level reflection of the frontend's failed requests rather than an independent proxy fault: they appear only in the same buckets as the frontend error burst, and the observed pre-incident topology is load-generator to frontend-proxy ingress to router frontend egress to frontend. No in-window proxy trace carrying error status details was available to confirm this.

The ad application itself reported no failures: its only ERROR spans in the window were 1.33 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean, and the readable ad container log lines in 14:53:11–14:55:14 are normal request-handling lines ("Targeted ad request received ...", "no baggage found in context") with no error text. This supports calls not reaching a listening ad rather than ad returning application errors.

Current cluster state does not show a damaged workload: every otel-demo deployment reports 1/1 ready and available, and the ad, payment and frontend pods are Running with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, so what the metrics show is a startup/rollout window rather than a crash loop.

Rejected: a frontend crash, restart or OOM caused the error rate. The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg has been running since 14:12:41Z with restartCount 0, and the errors are confined to its dependency client spans (GetAds, PlaceOrder, tcp.connect) rather than to its own startup.

Rejected: the ad container was crash-looping or OOM-killed. The ad pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 has restartCount 0 and an empty lastState on a single instance started at 14:45:29Z, and the returned events cover only Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started for the new pod and Killing, SuccessfulDelete for the old pod — no BackOff, Unhealthy or eviction event was observed.

Add a gRPC readiness probe (and a startup probe) on port 8080 to the ad container, and to payment, so the Service does not route traffic to an instance before "Ad service started, listening on 8080" and the gRPC server is bound; this is the specific setting that let a not-yet-listening pod be Ready from 14:45:29.

Raise the ad container's cpu limit above 50m or give the JVM a startup CPU boost, and review the rollout so the old ad pod is not deleted at 14:45:29 before the replacement can serve; with one replica this rollout left no serving instance for roughly six minutes.

Use the change-history integration to identify who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart of the ad (14:45:27Z) and payment (14:45:26Z) Deployments, and confirm the alert has resolved now that ad and payment are serving.

gaps: The cause of the rollout restarts themselves (ad at 14:45:27Z, payment at 14:45:26Z) is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change record, actor or commit could be read.

The alerting rule definition could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data with an empty result, so the exact RequestErrorRate expression and its window are unknown, and the annotation value 4.422% could not be reproduced from the available series (frontend error ratio 0.30% over 5m at 14:46:30, 1.51% over 1m, GET /api/data 8 errors of 122 spans = 6.56% over 1m).

Jaeger holds no traces newer than about 14:30Z for this target (newest sample starts 14:30:02.69Z) and traces_search_by_tags with error=true for frontend in 14:40–15:05:16 returned no_data, so the exact gRPC status codes and messages of the failing GetAds and Charge calls in the incident window are unknown; the fast-failure reading rests on span-duration buckets plus the absence of server spans.
The frontend container log could not be read: both fetch_pod_logs queries for frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg returned no_data with 0 lines read, so no frontend application error text is available.

A fetch_pod_logs query for the ad pod over 14:45:20–14:48:00 returned no_data (0 lines, all 218 retained lines reported after the window end), so it is a gap rather than a fact whether ad logged anything earlier than 14:50:09; the earliest returned ad log line is 14:50:09.97Z.

kube-state-metrics series were not present for this target (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and kube_pod_container_info returned no_data), so per-pod readiness history across the rollout could not be reconstructed; readiness evidence comes from pod status conditions observed after the fact.
traces_span_metrics series for these operations stop around 14:57–15:01Z, so the frontend error rate and alert state after that time, including whether the alert has resolved, are unknown.

Health of services that returned no ERROR series in the aggregate query (cart, currency, product-catalog, quote, shipping, email, accounting, fraud-detection) is unverified; their absence of error spans is not established as zero errors.
next_steps: Confirm from Alertmanager/Prometheus rule data (outside this Run's available sources) the exact RequestErrorRate expression and whether the alert resolved after ad resumed serving around 14:53Z.
Add readiness/startup probes to the ad and payment container specs and raise the ad CPU limit, then re-test a rollout to confirm zero failed GetAds calls.
Inspect cluster/CI change history for the 2026-11-16T14:45:26–27Z rollout restarts of deployments ad and payment to determine the triggering change.
Check a longer-retention trace backend for 14:45–14:56Z spans of frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds to capture the exact gRPC error code (for example UNAVAILABLE) as confirmation.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
